setup.description:
Fixture repo built via libgit2 directly`): libgit2 in a fresh temp dir; `user.name`/`user.email` set locally; `core.autocrlf` set to false so checked-out content is byte-identical regardless of the host's global autocrlf. Commit 1 ('initial'): a.txt = 'one
' on the default branch (captured as `base`, whatever the host's default branch name is — not assumed to be 'main'). A branch named 'feature' is created from that commit and checked out. Commit 2 ('feature edit'): a.txt = 'feature
', committed on 'feature'. The fixture then checks back out to `base`, leaving a.txt = 'one
' in the working tree and HEAD on `base`.

steps: write 'uncommitted work\n' to a.txt on disk, without staging it
cases.notes: The uncommitted edit to a.txt collides with what checking out 'feature' would need to overwrite (a.txt also differs on 'feature'), so libgit2's safe checkout returns ErrorCode::Conflict, which checkout_error tags with the verbatim CHECKOUT_CONFLICT_PREFIX. The suffix after the prefix is libgit2's own English message and is not asserted byte-for-byte by the original test (assert!(err.starts_with(...))) — only the prefix is a contract.

steps: write 'uncommitted work\n' to a.txt on disk, without staging it
call checkout_local_branch(repo_path, "feature") — assert it errors (same conflict as the case above)
cases.notes: Verifies the frontend's actual recovery path for GIT-003/CHECKOUT_CONFLICT_PREFIX: stashing the blocking uncommitted change (repoStore.ts's checkoutGuarded calls stashSave then retries the same checkout) unblocks the identical checkout call. The stash itself is left in place afterward (not popped) — the test only asserts the checkout now succeeds and exactly one stash exists.
